title: Homotopically injective DG resolutions and their localization comparison
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. A differential graded algebra over $\mathbf Z$ means an associative unital graded ring $A=\bigoplus_{i\in\mathbf Z}A^i$ with additive differential $d:A^i\to A^{i+1}$ satisfying $d^2=0$ and $d(ab)=d(a)b+(-1)^ia\,d(b)$ for $a\in A^i$. A right differential graded $A$-module is a graded right module $M$ with $d^2=0$ and $d(ma)=d(m)a+(-1)^jm\,d(a)$ for $m\in M^j$. Write $D(A,d)$ for the homotopy category of these modules localized at the maps inducing isomorphisms on all cohomology groups; triangles are the distinguished mapping-cone triangles. For right DG modules $X,Y$ write $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(X,Y)^r$ for degree-$r$ graded right $A$-linear maps, with differential $df=d_Yf-(-1)^rfd_X$. Write $K(A,d)$ for DG modules with morphisms $H^0\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(X,Y)$; its localization functor is $Q_A:K(A,d)\to D(A,d)$. Call $I$ homotopically injective if $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(C,I)$ is acyclic for every acyclic right DG $A$-module $C$. Every right DG $A$-module $Y$ admits a quasi-isomorphism $Y\to I$ with $I$ homotopically injective. For every such $I$ and every right DG module $X$, localization induces a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{K(A,d)}(X,I)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A,d)}(Q_AX,Q_AI)$. These bijections are natural in both variables. Shifts of homotopically injective modules are homotopically injective. No boundedness or flatness assumption is imposed.

proof.text: Set $M_0=Y$. Inductively apply [lem-sfb-dg-good-character-embedding] to $M_i$, obtaining $u_i:M_i\hookrightarrow E_i$, and put $M_{i+1}=E_i/u_i(M_i)$. Define $f_i:E_i\to E_{i+1}$ by quotient followed by $u_{i+1}$. Thus $0\to Y\to E_0\to E_1\to\cdots$ is exact degree by degree. Write $E_i^{\prime}\subset E_i$ for the graded-split DG submodule furnished by that node; both $E_i^{\prime}$ and $E_i/E_i^{\prime}$ are products of shifts of $A^\vee$. This specifies the induction base, step and all horizontal maps.

source.place: Tag 09KU, lemma-right-resolution, first paragraph; Tag 09KT, lemma-good-sub.

proof.text: For each $n$ put $c_n(V)=V^n/d_V(V^{n-1})$. For $0\to M_i\to E_i\to M_{i+1}\to0$, the sequence $c_n(M_i)\to c_n(E_i)\to c_n(M_{i+1})\to0$ is right exact: lift an element in degree $n$; if its image is a boundary, lift a preimage in degree $n-1$ and subtract its differential. The first arrow is injective by [lem-sfb-dg-good-character-embedding]. Splicing these short exact sequences proves exactness of all augmented cokernel rows. Apply [lem-sfb-good-coresolution-product-total] to the underlying abelian-group complexes. It gives a quasi-isomorphism $Y\to I$, where $I^n=\prod_{i\ge0}E_i^{n-i}$ and $(d_Ix)_i=f_{i-1}(x_{i-1})+(-1)^i d_{E_i}x_i$ (first term zero for $i=0$). Give $I$ the coordinatewise right action. The two mixed terms in $d_I^2$ cancel since $f_i$ commutes with $d$; $f_if_{i-1}=0$ kills the horizontal square. For $x\in I^n$, the internal Leibniz term has sign $(-1)^i(-1)^{n-i}=(-1)^n$, proving the DG Leibniz rule. The augmentation $(u_0,0,\ldots)$ is DG-linear and a chain map.

source.place: Tag 09KU, product-total construction and final quasi-isomorphism argument; homology.tex Tag 09J0.

proof.text: Define $F_{2i}I^n$ by $x_j=0$ for $j<i$, and $F_{2i+1}I^n$ by the same equations plus $x_i\in(E_i^{\prime})^{n-i}$. These are DG submodules: horizontal differentials only increase $j$, and $E_i^{\prime}$ is a DG submodule. Their successive quotients are $(E_i/E_i^{\prime})[-i]$ and $E_i^{\prime}[-i]$. They are products of shifts of $A^\vee$ by Step 1. The quotient transition maps split after forgetting differentials by coordinate sections and the graded splitting in [lem-sfb-dg-good-character-embedding]. Compatible finite truncations specify each coordinate exactly once, so $I\to\varprojlim I/F_pI$ is an isomorphism. Apply [lem-sfb-dg-complete-cofree-orthogonality] to this filtration and to each shifted filtration $F_p(I[r])=(F_pI)[r]$; shifting preserves all displayed products, splittings and quotients. For acyclic $C$ it gives $\operatorname{Hom}_{K(A,d)}(C,I[r])=0$ for every $r$. The identity on homogeneous maps identifies $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(C,I[r])$ with $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(C,I)[r]$, including the differential $(-1)^r d$. Hence $H^r\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(C,I)=0$ for all $r$: $I$ is homotopically injective.

source.place: Tags 09KU and 09KS; corrected odd filtration indexing in lemma-right-resolution; all-shifts application of lemma-property-I-K-injective.

proof.text: For an arbitrary homotopically injective $J$, the definition gives $\operatorname{Hom}_{K(A,d)}(C,J)=H^0\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(C,J)=0$ for every acyclic $C$. By [lem-sfb-dg-homotopy-acyclic-localization], $K(A,d)$ is triangulated, its acyclic modules form a strictly full triangulated subcategory $\mathcal E$, and its cone class $W_{\mathcal E}$ is exactly the quasi-isomorphisms. Thus $Q_A$ is a localization at that cone class. Apply [lem-sfb-right-orthogonal-localization-hom] to $J$, $Q_A$ and $X$. Its bijection is precisely $f\mapsto Q_A(f)$, proving the comparison for every homotopically injective target, without requiring the filtration of Step 3.

source.place: Tag 09KY, lemma-hom-derived, dual cone-and-localization argument for (2); generic right-orthogonal theorem in Mathlib/Triangulated/Orthogonal.lean:108.

proof.text: For $a:X\prime\to X$ and a map $b:J\to J\prime$ between homotopically injective targets, functoriality gives $Q_A(bfa)=Q_A(b)Q_A(f)Q_A(a)$. This proves naturality of the comparison bijections in both variables; their inverses are natural by uniqueness. For arbitrary $J$ and $r$, the same identity of Hom complexes used in Step 3 gives $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(C,J[r])=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(C,J)[r]$. Its cohomology in degree $n$ is $H^{n+r}\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(C,J)=0$, so every shift of $J$ is homotopically injective. Products throughout range over $i\ge0$ and over sets of homogeneous characters, allowed by the fixed universe convention; no degree support or flatness was used.

lean.statement: theorem dg_injective_resolution_localization (A : Algebra.{u}) : (∀ Y : RightModule A, ∃ (I : RightModule A) (i : Y ⟶ I), quasiIsomorphisms A i ∧ IsHomotopicallyInjective A I) ∧ (∃ L : HomotopyCategory A ⥤ Derived A, homotopyQuotient A ⋙ L = Q A ∧ ∀ (X I : RightModule A), IsHomotopicallyInjective A I → Function.Bijective (L.map : ((homotopyQuotient A).obj X ⟶ (homotopyQuotient A).obj I) → (L.obj ((homotopyQuotient A).obj X) ⟶ L.obj ((homotopyQuotient A).obj I)))) ∧ (∀ I : RightModule A, IsHomotopicallyInjective A I → ∀ (r : ℤ) (S : RightModule A), ShiftComparison A r I S → IsHomotopicallyInjective A S)
